Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is a focused proposal that ties committed throughput to an operational ramp and burst plan so BlueHarbor can hit your Q4 latency targets while keeping unit economics predictable. High-level options included in BH-Dedicated-Proposal-v3.pdf (attached) and the accompanying cost workbook (cluster-cost-model.xlsx):

Option A — Conservative anchor
- Committed baseline: 8 GPUs (A100/80GB or equivalent)
- Minimum concurrent guarantee: 6 GPUs for 99% of traffic windows
- Ramp: 6 -> 8 over 60 days after go-live (linear weekly increments)
- Burst pool: up to +50% capacity (4 GPUs) billed at a premium burst rate when used
- Expected steady-state latency: 25–40ms median token generation for your 1.2k seq use-case
- Price: $X/hour committed; burst @ +35% premium

Option B — Performance anchor (recommended for high-concurrency search)
- Committed baseline: 16 GPUs
- Minimum concurrent guarantee: 12 GPUs
- Ramp: 12 -> 16 over 30 days (frontloaded)
- Burst pool: +50% usable; burst credits included for first 3 months
- Price: $Y/hour committed; favorable long-run unit cost

Option C — Flex anchor (short-term test/POC)
- Committed baseline: 4 GPUs (30-day pilot)
- Minimum guarantee: 2 GPUs
- Ramp: 30-day pilot then convert to A/B depending on performance/usage
- Burst pool: limited (on-demand)
- Price: higher per-GPU hour to reflect short-term reservations

Key trade-offs and notes:
- Minimum concurrent guarantee (min GPUs) is about stabilizing tail latency during traffic spikes without overcommitting reserve capacity.
- Burst pool is implemented as pre-warmed nodes that can be leased at higher rate; availability is subject to regional capacity but we include cross-region fallback policies in the proposal.
- We included an optional 10% first-year usage credit for customers that sign a 12-month reserved commitment (see pricing appendix).

Next steps I recommend:
1) You confirm which option (A/B/C) is closest to your appetite for cost vs. latency.
2) Procurement can review the attached T&Cs; if the procurement team prefers, we can issue a draft SOW with explicit SLA language and ramp milestones.
3) If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min technical run-through with our infra lead (Karthik) to validate perf numbers against your real prompt set.
